module booth_multiplier #(parameter N = 4) (
    input wire [N-1:0] A,
    input wire [N-1:0] B,
    output reg [2*N-1:0] P
);
    reg [N-1:0] M, Q;
    reg Q_1;
    reg [N:0] A_ext, P_temp;
    integer i;

    always @(*) begin
        M = A;          // Multiplicand
        Q = B;          // Multiplier
        Q_1 = 1'b0;    // Previous Q bit
        A_ext = {1'b0, M}; // Extend A to N+1 bits
        P_temp = {N+1{1'b0}}; // Initialize product to 0
        P_temp[N:0] = {Q, Q_1}; // Combine Q and Q-1
        
        for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
            case ({Q[0], Q_1})
                2'b01: P_temp = P_temp + A_ext; // Add M
                2'b10: P_temp = P_temp - A_ext; // Subtract M
                default: P_temp = P_temp; // Do nothing
            endcase
            Q_1 = Q[0]; // Update previous Q bit
            Q = {P_temp[N], Q[N-1:1]}; // Shift right
            P_temp[N] = P_temp[N-1]; // Maintain sign bit
        end
        
        P = P_temp[N:1]; // Final product
    end

The tree structure will be defined using a set of register values representing node values. The traversal should be initiated by a start signal.

module DFS_BinaryTree (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire start,
    input wire [7:0] node_value,
    output reg [7:0] dfs_output,
    output reg done
);
    reg [3:0] state;
    reg [15:0] stack [0:15]; // Stack for DFS
    reg [3:0] sp; // Stack pointer

    parameter IDLE = 0, PUSH = 1, POP = 2, OUTPUT = 3;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            sp <= 0;
            done <= 0;
            dfs_output <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        stack[sp] <= node_value; // Push the root node
                        sp <= sp + 1;
                        state <= PUSH;
                    end
                end
                PUSH: begin
                    if (sp > 0) begin
                        dfs_output <= stack[sp - 1]; // Output the top of the stack
                        sp <= sp - 1; // Pop the stack
                        state <= OUTPUT;
                    end else begin
                        done <= 1; // No more nodes to process
                        state <= IDLE; // Go back to IDLE
                    end
                end
                OUTPUT: begin
                    state <= PUSH; // Go back to pushing next node
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

module SRT_Divider (
    input [15:0] dividend,
    input [15:0] divisor,
    output reg [15:0] quotient,
    output reg [15:0] remainder
);

always @(*) begin
    if (divisor == 16'b0) begin
        quotient = 16'b0; // Avoid division by zero
        remainder = dividend; // Remainder is the dividend
    end else begin
        quotient = dividend / divisor; // Simple integer division
        remainder = dividend % divisor; // Remainder
    end
end

endmodule

description:
Design a simple SATA controller state machine that manages the initialization and data transfer states. The controller should have the following states: IDLE, INIT, and DATA. The transitions are:
- From IDLE to INIT when a start signal is asserted.
- From INIT to DATA when initialization is complete.
- From DATA to IDLE when data transfer is complete.
The controller should output the current state as a 2-bit value: 00 for IDLE, 01 for INIT, and 10 for DATA.
code:
module sata_controller (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input start,
    input init_done,
    input data_done,
    output reg [1:0] state
);
    // State encoding
    localparam IDLE = 2'b00;
    localparam INIT = 2'b01;
    localparam DATA = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        state <= INIT;
                    end
                end
                INIT: begin
                    if (init_done) begin
                        state <= DATA;
                    end
                end
                DATA: begin
                    if (data_done) begin
                        state <= IDLE;
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

1. If X1 == 1, go to the left child (return Y = 1 if X2 == 1).
2. If X1 == 0, go to the right child (return Y = 0 if X3 == 0).

    input wire X1,
    input wire X2,
    input wire X3,
    output reg Y
);

        if (X1) begin
            if (X2) begin
                Y = 1; // Path: X1==1, X2==1
            end else begin
                Y = 0; // Path: X1==1, X2==0
            end
        end else begin
            if (X3) begin
                Y = 1; // Path: X1==0, X3==1
            end else begin
                Y = 0; // Path: X1==0, X3==0
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description:
Design a Verilog module that simulates a simple SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) system. The system should take in position and map updates at each clock cycle and maintain an internal state representing the current position and an array representing the map. The inputs are:
- `clk`: clock signal
- `reset`: reset signal
- `position_update`: a 2-bit position input that indicates the movement direction (00: no movement, 01: move left, 10: move right, 11: move forward)
- `map_update`: a 5-bit value representing a new obstacle detected in the map.

The output is:
- `current_position`: a 2-bit output representing the current position of the entity.
- `map`: a 32-bit output representing the current state of the map (occupied or free).

The map is represented as a 32-bit register, where each bit corresponds to a cell in the environment. The position indicates the current index of the entity in this map, and the position updates will change this index accordingly.
code:
module slam_system (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [1:0] position_update,
    input [4:0] map_update,
    output reg [1:0] current_position,
    output reg [31:0] map
);

always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        current_position <= 2'b00; // Reset position
        map <= 32'b0; // Reset map
    end else begin
        // Update current_position based on position_update
        case (position_update)
            2'b00: current_position <= current_position; // No movement
            2'b01: current_position <= current_position - 1; // Move left
            2'b10: current_position <= current_position + 1; // Move right
            2'b11: current_position <= current_position; // Move forward
        endcase

        // Update map based on map_update
        map[current_position] <= 1'b1; // Mark the current position in the map
    end
end

endmodule

description: Design a Verilog module that implements a simplified version of the Bellman-Ford algorithm to find the shortest path in a graph represented by an adjacency matrix. The module should take the number of vertices, the weight matrix, and an initial source vertex as inputs, and output the shortest distances from the source to all other vertices.
code:
module bellman_ford #(parameter N = 5) (  
    input [N*N-1:0] weights, // NxN weight matrix flattened  
    input [2:0] source,      // source vertex (0 to N-1)  
    output reg [N*8-1:0] distances // distances array (8 bits for each vertex)  
);  
    integer i, j, k;  
    reg [7:0] dist [0:N-1];  

    always @(*) begin  
        // Initialize distances  
        for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin  
            dist[i] = 8'hFF; // Set to infinity  
        end  
        dist[source] = 8'h00; // Distance to self is 0  

        // Relax edges up to N-1 times  
        for (k = 0; k < N-1; k = k + 1) begin  
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin  
                for (j = 0; j < N; j = j + 1) begin  
                    if (weights[i*N+j] != 8'hFF && dist[i] != 8'hFF) begin  
                        if (dist[i] + weights[i*N+j] < dist[j]) begin  
                            dist[j] = dist[i] + weights[i*N+j];  
                        end  
                    end  
                end  
            end  
        end  

        // Pack distances into output  
        for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin  
            distances[i*8 +: 8] = dist[i];  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

Design a 64-bit ALU that can perform basic arithmetic and logical operations including addition, subtraction, bitwise AND, bitwise OR, and bitwise XOR based on a 3-bit operation selector. The ALU should take two 64-bit inputs and output a 64-bit result. The operation selector works as follows: 
000 - Addition
001 - Subtraction
010 - Bitwise AND
011 - Bitwise OR
100 - Bitwise XOR
The ALU also has a zero flag output that indicates if the result is zero.
code:
module ALU_64bit (
    input [63:0] A,
    input [63:0] B,
    input [2:0] op_sel,
    output reg [63:0] result,
    output reg zero
);
    always @(*) begin
        case(op_sel)
            3'b000: result = A + B;          // Addition
            3'b001: result = A - B;          // Subtraction
            3'b010: result = A & B;          // Bitwise AND
            3'b011: result = A | B;          // Bitwise OR
            3'b100: result = A ^ B;          // Bitwise XOR
            default: result = 64'b0;
        endcase
        zero = (result == 64'b0);
    end
endmodule

description: Design a non-restoring divider in Verilog that takes an 8-bit dividend and an 8-bit divisor as inputs and produces a 16-bit quotient and a 8-bit remainder. The division should be performed in a non-restoring manner, with the input values being provided to the divider and the results being ready after a few clock cycles. You should handle division by zero gracefully, setting the quotient to 0 and the remainder to the dividend in that case.
code:
module non_restoring_divider (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [7:0] dividend,
    input [7:0] divisor,
    input start,
    output reg [15:0] quotient,
    output reg [7:0] remainder,
    output reg done
);

    reg [15:0] A; // Accumulator
    reg [7:0] B; // Divisor
    reg [4:0] count;
    reg state; // 0: idle, 1: busy

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            A <= 0;
            B <= 0;
            count <= 0;
            quotient <= 0;
            remainder <= 0;
            done <= 0;
            state <= 0;
        end else if (start && state == 0) begin
            // Initialize A and B
            A <= {8'b0, dividend}; // Load dividend
            B <= divisor;          // Load divisor
            quotient <= 0;        // Clear quotient
            remainder <= 0;       // Clear remainder
            count <= 8;          // Set count for 8 bits
            state <= 1;          // Set state to busy
            done <= 0;
        end else if (state == 1) begin
            if (count > 0) begin
                A <= {A[14:0], 1'b0}; // Shift A left
                if (A[15:8] >= B) begin
                    A <= A - {B, 8'b0}; // Subtract B
                    quotient <= {quotient[14:0], 1'b1}; // Append 1 to quotient
                end else begin
                    quotient <= {quotient[14:0], 1'b0}; // Append 0 to quotient
                end
                count <= count - 1; // Decrement count
            end else begin
                remainder <= A[7:0]; // Remainder is the last 8 bits of A
                state <= 0;          // Set state back to idle
                done <= 1;           // Indicate done
            end
        end
    end
endmodule
